name: kalibrate
description: One memory for every AI tool on your team. Facts show who checked them and when.

interface.shortDescription: Team memory for your AI tools
interface.longDescription:
Kalibrate is one shared memory for a software team that uses more than one AI tool. ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, VS Code and Gemini CLI all connect to the same server, so a note saved from one tool can be recalled from any other.

What you can do from ChatGPT or Codex:
- Recall team memory. Ask before you act. You get a verdict first (clear, stale, conflict or unknown), then the facts, notes and what teammates are working on.
- Remember a note. Save something worth keeping. Notes are private unless you save them to the team.
- Verify a fact. Mark that you checked a fact's source and it still holds, or record the new value.
- Track work. Claim a task before you start. You get a warning if someone is on overlapping work. Finish it, or hand it over.
- List open items. What is waiting on you or the team, who owns it and how it closes.
- Settle an item. Retire a note, dismiss an item, pass it to its owner, or undo.
- Share to the team. Copy one of your private notes to the team, only after you say yes.

Every fact carries a sticker: who checked it and when. An answer checked ten minutes ago looks different from one nobody has looked at since last month.

Who it's for: software teams of 3 to 15 people where most people use AI agents daily and the team uses two or more different AI tools on the same work. People who don't write code are welcome too. A founder in ChatGPT can read what a developer's agent saved from Codex.

Limitations:
- You need a Kalibrate account. Sign in with Google or an email and password when you first connect.
- When two people save different values for the same fact, the second value is refused unless it comes from a more trusted source. Holding both open for a person to decide is not built yet.
- Track work records what an agent says it is doing and has done. Kalibrate does not check that the work was really done.
- Kalibrate stores text and links, not files.
- It refuses notes that look like secrets or keys. Store a pointer to your secret manager instead.
- It stores only what you and your agents save to it. It does not read your ChatGPT memory or chat history.

It's early. Tell us where it breaks.
